constructionScope_hypothetical_hsr: Build a hypothetical high-speed line via Carcassonne.
title: World-wide High-speed Rail Tycoon
selectCity: Choose a city on the map or in the list.
hint: Your Tokyo–Nagoya starter service is ready to earn revenue. Advance a month, tune fares in Services, or compare two new construction opportunities in Build a line.
reportHint: Tickets are collected when a month closes. Construction and grants are capital flows, separate from operating profit.
noReport: Advance a month to close your first report.
soundless: This early build has no sound.
stale_revision: The game changed. Review the latest state and try again.
storage_failed: Could not save. Your previous game is intact. Free some space and retry.
invalid_save: The saved game is invalid or belongs to a different build. It has been preserved.
locked: This game is open in another tab. Close that tab and reload here.
storageUnavailable: Local storage is unavailable. Enable storage for this site and reload.
action_limit: This development game has reached its action limit. Export your snapshot to keep it.
buildHint: When the line opens, lease trains here and apply a service plan to earn revenue.
estimateNote: Scenario engineering estimates. Tunnels cost more; detours take longer.
no_route: No authored alignment for this pair. Choose a listed construction opportunity.
already_built: This line is public, owned, or already under construction.
insufficient_cash: Not enough cash. Review financing in Company.
line_not_open: This line is still under construction.
invalid_service: Use 0–16 return trips/day and a USD 10–300 one-way fare.
fleet_shortage: Lease enough trains on this corridor or reduce frequency.
fleet_in_use: Reduce frequency before returning this train.
loan_limit: The development loan limit is USD 5B.
cash_limit: This action exceeds the development cash limit.
set_service: Service plan saved. Advance the month to settle fares and costs.
advance_year: Twelve business months resolved and saved.
serviceHint: One return trip is one departure each way. Shared public capacity is provisional until resolution. Shorter rides pay by distance. Frequency 0 suspends a service.
forecastCosts: Operating costs, required leases and line upkeep
loanTerms: Borrow any amount within the remaining USD 5B credit limit at 2% annual interest. Cash overdrafts incur 1% monthly interest. Borrowing always requires your action.
noServices: No services on this corridor yet.
draft_not_applied: Service draft is not applied. Apply or restore the current plan before advancing.
invalid_loan_amount: Enter a positive USD amount with up to two decimal places.
terrainCredits: Terrain: Mapzen / USGS; water: Natural Earth; rail: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)
hokkaidoMountainWhy: The shorter northern approach crosses the Oshima and Shiribeshi uplands: this scenario needs 170 km of tunnel.
hokkaidoValleyWhy: The longer coastal/Chitose approach skirts the central uplands. It still needs 45 km of tunnel; the detour is not mountain-free.
kansaiMountainWhy: A shorter crossing through the highlands west of Lake Biwa; this scenario needs 140 km of tunnel.
kansaiValleyWhy: The longer route follows Lake Biwa’s eastern and southern shores instead of crossing the lake. This scenario still needs 20 km of tunnel.
idleExplanation: These owned lines or service fleets are idle while upkeep and lease costs continue. A shared line may have other trains; an idle leased fleet still costs money.
idleNeedsTrains: Lease trains and apply a service.
idleNeedsService: Trains are leased. Apply a service with a frequency above zero.
newGameWarning: This replaces your current company and save, including all lines, loans, trains and reports. This cannot be undone.
newGameStart: Start in East Asia in January 2029 with USD 100 million and an active Tokyo–Nagoya service. Display preferences are kept.
fundingFormula: Your contribution − cash available + any cash deficit = additional cash needed (minimum USD 0).
fundingNegativeCash: Your cash balance is negative, so this includes clearing the existing deficit.
fundingLoanHelp: Borrow funding shortfall takes this full amount in one loan. You can enter a different loan amount below.
fundingChoosePlan: Choose an unbuilt line in Build a line to see its funding breakdown.
shortfallInterest: Monthly interest added by borrowing the full gap
stationHandling: Station handling / service boarding · both ends
directService: A direct service runs between this city pair. Another corridor needs its own service.
stationAbsent: No station yet · included when a new line opens
stationPackage: Basic endpoint station works open with this project and are included in this introductory package. No separate station order is needed.
helpFirstMonth: Your starter trains are ready. Advance one month to collect fares and see a reconciled report. You can also plan a new line immediately.
helpIdle: An owned line or leased service fleet is idle. Review it, start a service, or return spare trains to stop avoidable lease costs.
helpPair: Pick a dotted construction prospect or its named list entry, then compare alignments. Either endpoint can be outside the existing network.
helpConstruction: Track and endpoint station works open together on the stated date. Each month also settles your operating costs and income.
helpOpen: This line and its stations are ready. Review its service, lease the required trains, and apply a fare and frequency.
helpPublic: This public line is already operational. You can lease trains and run a service without buying the track.
helpFunding: Compare the engineering and funding breakdown. Company financing can cover the full displayed shortfall in one loan.
helpBuildReady: Your cash covers the construction contribution. Starting construction commits the project package and its stated opening date.
helpFleet: Lease trains for this service pattern before applying it, or use the starter extension to transfer its fleet.
helpDraft: These are draft settings. Check the fleet requirement and forecast, then apply the plan or restore the saved settings before advancing.
helpSuspended: Frequency zero suspends this service. Any leased trains and owned-line upkeep still cost money; resume service or return spare trains.
helpOperating: This plan is saved for the next month. Advancing collects fares and posts track access, station handling, train leases and running costs.
helpLoss: This month’s operating costs exceeded ticket income. Review service demand, fares, fleet and idle-line costs before advancing again.
helpReport: The report separates ticket income and operating costs from loans, grants and construction. Closing cash reconciles all of them.
helpFinance: The funding preview names its route and alignment. Review that route to change the plan; borrowing is a separate explicit action.
helpCompany: Company finances are shared by every line. Services show what your fleet can earn before company-wide interest.
helpExplore: Inspect stations and compare the build opportunities. A new city pair can operate independently of your existing railway.
helpFinished: This campaign is complete. Company lets you start a new game.
helpFunded: Your cash covers this construction package. Review the route, then start construction when you are ready.
helpBuiltOperating: This line and its stations are open, with a saved running service. Review its fares, frequency and fleet as demand changes.
networkService: Services can share track and run through several cities. Fares for shorter rides are proportional to kilometres; a transfer adds a wait and uses another service.
extendStarter: Extend Tokyo–Nagoya to Osaka; move its trains
deliveredFrequency: Delivered / requested return trips per day
noNetworkReport: Advance a month to resolve the network and its representative day. Older reports keep their original accounts.
railRejected: Rail requests returned to outside modes
invalid_extension: Choose an unused longer service pattern containing the source service and its called stations.
track_capacity: The requested service frequencies exceed track capacity. See the section and service breakdown.
station_capacity: The requested service frequencies exceed station capacity. See the station and service breakdown.
extend_service: Through service applied; trains transferred and listed leases started.
helpExtension: The extension replaces your starter service, moves its trains and leases only the displayed extra trains. Review the monthly lease total and company-wide change, then apply.
learnSummary_getting_started: Start with the cheapest construction prospect. If it is out of reach, run service on an open line and advance the month to collect fares.
learnDetail_getting_started: Months settle only when you use the time controls. A forecast is an estimate; the monthly report records what actually happened. You can explore the map and change drafts without advancing time.
learnSummary_city_demand: A large city offers potential passengers, but travel time, fares and competing modes determine who rides.
learnDetail_city_demand: Select a city to inspect its station. Resolved passenger markets show actual demand and journeys; population alone is not a revenue guarantee. A station and an open, usable route are both needed to run trains.
learnSummary_connections: Pick a dotted prospect on the map or choose it from the list, then compare alignments.
learnDetail_connections: Only supported, unstarted corridors appear as dotted prospects. Select the whole line to review its endpoints, alignment, cost and operating forecast. The selected alignment is highlighted. Starting construction removes the prospect and shows the accepted project instead. Expand the map to browse without losing your draft.
learnSummary_terrain: Tunnels, viaducts and difficult terrain can make a shorter alignment more expensive. Compare cost, opening date and journey time.
learnDetail_terrain: The engineering breakdown includes regional construction costs and the station package. Terrain shading explains the detours; it is not a route editor. A faster alignment may attract more riders, but its higher capital cost still needs financing.
learnSummary_funding: Additional cash needed is your construction contribution minus cash, including any existing cash deficit.
learnDetail_funding: The public grant reduces the project price you must fund. A loan supplies cash and increases debt and monthly interest; it does not reduce construction cost. The exact-gap shortcut borrows only the quoted shortfall, subject to your credit limit.
learnSummary_construction: Construction takes game months. When a line opens, assign trains and apply a service so it can earn revenue.
learnDetail_construction: The opening date belongs to the accepted project. Advancing a year resolves twelve operating months with all their costs. Open lines incur maintenance even without passengers, so prepare fleet and service plans before opening.
learnSummary_fleet: Required trains depend on frequency and the full round trip, including turnaround. Leasing alone does not apply a service.
learnDetail_fleet: The forecast shows assigned and required trains for this draft. Each leased train has a monthly charge, even when idle. Apply the timetable after providing enough trains; an extension can move the starter fleet and lease the quoted extra trains together.
learnSummary_service_plans: Frequency and fare edits are drafts. Apply the service to change the trains that actually run.
learnDetail_service_plans: Forecasts evaluate the current draft against the operating network. Restore plan discards your edits and returns to the accepted service. Time controls warn about unapplied drafts so a preview is not mistaken for an operating timetable. Click operating track on the map to open Services, then choose a direct or through route along that track. Show all service routes clears the map filter. New service plans use route-based starting fares and frequencies. Existing accepted plans stay unchanged until you apply edits.
learnSummary_fares_demand: Higher fares can reduce riders. Compare operating contribution and the change across your whole company.
learnDetail_fares_demand: Operating contribution is this service’s revenue minus its operating costs. Company change also captures passengers diverted from, or fed to, your other services. Forecasts are estimates, not promised cash; compare them with the next monthly report. Operating costs include leased trains even when they have spare capacity. The main forecast shows monthly break-even riders; Analysis explains the costs and the fixed-fare, fixed-passenger-mix assumption.
learnSummary_through_services: A through service uses one train over several connected sections and serves the listed intermediate stops.
learnDetail_through_services: Tokyo–Nagoya–Osaka lets passengers stay on the same train. Extending the starter service replaces that accepted service and moves its trains; creating a separate service leaves both running. Review extra leases and company change before applying.
learnSummary_capacity: Requested frequency may exceed the paths available on a shared section. Delivered frequency shows what can actually run.
learnDetail_capacity: Through services consume capacity on every section they use. The network report identifies constrained sections and unmet demand. More trains cannot create extra track paths; adjust frequencies or redistribute services.
learnSummary_monthly_report: Reconcile passenger revenue, operating costs and financing separately to understand the closing cash balance.
learnDetail_monthly_report: Revenue minus total operating costs shows operating cash generation. Construction, grants, borrowing and repayments also change cash but are not ticket income. Open the network report to inspect transfers, feeder journeys, unmet demand and section capacity.
learnSummary_idle_assets: An open line without operating trains still costs money. Review the line’s accepted service and assigned fleet.
learnDetail_idle_assets: Idle warnings reflect actual accepted operations, not a draft. Leasing trains without applying a positive-frequency service may leave the line idle. Deliberate suspension remains possible; maintenance and lease costs continue.
learnSummary_operating_day: The animated operating day illustrates resolved services. Playing or scrubbing it does not advance the business month.
learnDetail_operating_day: Select a train to inspect its route, stops and progress. This is a representative day derived from the last settlement, not a live dispatch simulation. It cannot earn additional money or alter the accepted timetable.
noHelpResults: No matching topics. Try another term.
learnOriginCarried: Resolved rail passengers from this city
learnFleetDayMinutes: Available minutes per train per day
capacityMaxDraft: At most %d daily return trips with the other services unchanged.
capacityTrackWhy: Each return trip uses one path on every section of its route, including through and express services. Reduce this draft or the listed services to fit the limit. Extra trains do not increase track capacity.
capacityStationWhy: Each return trip makes two calls at every served station, one in each direction. Reduce frequency on the listed stopping services. Express services that skip this station do not use its call capacity.
workspaceResponsive: Narrow windows use top navigation and a full-width task panel. Your desktop layout is remembered.
noMarket: No company rail service for this pair.
sourceStationInfo: Mapped station. Service plans use the city hubs in the route selector.
sourceStationGap: Known map gap: this marker alone does not establish a rail connection.
existingPublicConnection: An existing public railway connects these cities. You can run trains on it and pay access fees.
planExistingService: Plan trains on this existing line
prospectHint: Select a construction prospect to review its alignment and cost.
noProspects: All supported prospects are already under construction or operating.
mapServiceHint: Click operating track on the map to choose a service route.
breakEvenAssumptions: Break-even holds the fare and forecast passenger mix constant. It includes running, access, handling, train leases and line upkeep; financing and construction payments are separate. Through-service riders may make shorter trips. It is a target, not a promise of demand.
breakEvenUnavailable: No useful break-even target at this frequency, fare or passenger mix.
connectorHint: This route includes slower connecting track between high-speed sections.
constructionScope_upgrade: Build higher-speed replacement works, priced as new construction.
constructionScope_dedicated_hsr: Build new dedicated HSR; the existing upgraded conventional line remains available.
authoredAlignmentNote: Strategic engineering estimate; detailed design and land acquisition are outside this estimate.
routeChoicesMore: Showing %d of %d routes. Zoom in or search to narrow the list.
routeChoicesNone: No route fits in this map view. Zoom out or search by name.
routeChoicesMoreRegion: Showing %d of %d routes. Choose a smaller region or search to narrow the list.
routeChoicesNoneRegion: No route fits in this region. Choose another region or search by name.
routeChoicesMoreSearch: Showing %d of %d matching routes. Add a word to the search to narrow the list.
routeChoicesNoneSearch: No route matches. Change or clear the search.
zeroBestFrequency: Zero trips gives the best forecast at this fare. Try another fare or line.
frequencyOptimized: Best frequency at this fare is in the plan. Review the forecast before applying.
noFeasibleFrequency: No feasible frequency at this fare.
